label: STOPP D4: anticholinergic antipsychotic with prostate symptoms or urine retention
title: Antipsychotic with strong anticholinergic effects and prostate or urine retention problems
statement: Antipsychotics with moderate-marked antimuscarinic/anticholinergic effects (acepromazine, chlorpromazine, clozapine, flupenthixol, fluphenzine, levomepromazine, olanzapine, pipothiazine, promazine, thioridazine) with a history of lower urinary tract symptoms associated with benign prostatic hyperplasia or previous urinary retention (high risk of urinary retention).

source.document: O'Mahony D, et al. STOPP/START criteria for potentially inappropriate prescribing in older people: version 3. Eur Geriatr Med 2023;14:625-632, Appendix 1 (corrected supplementary file; NHS Somerset copy used for text, sentence-identical to the earlier parse)

plain_summary: Some antipsychotics block a nerve signal that helps the bladder empty, so they can cause urine retention in a man with prostate symptoms or anyone who has had urine retention before.

medicine_groups.name: Antipsychotics with moderate to marked anticholinergic effects
medicine_groups.note: These are the medicines the statement names. Match flupenthixol to flupentixol and pipothiazine to pipotiazine. The statement also spells fluphenazine as fluphenzine. Match acepromazine, pipotiazine and promazine by ingredient name. Long-acting injections count. The statement gives no way to rank other antipsychotics, so none are added. Generic packs that show the ingredient name with a company name count too.

needs_facts.what: History of urinary symptoms from an enlarged prostate or urinary retention
needs_facts.meets: A condition line records benign prostatic hyperplasia with urinary symptoms, or urinary retention (current or past).

options.words: Urinary symptoms from an enlarged prostate, now or in the past
Urinary retention, now or in the past

rule_for_models: Apply this rule only to people aged 65 years or older and confirm any unknown age before reporting a finding. When a Group A antipsychotic is supplied and a condition line confirms a history of urinary symptoms from benign prostate enlargement or a history of urinary retention, even if the symptoms or retention have resolved, suspect a finding and cite the supply and condition lines. With a Group A supply and neither history documented, report a possible finding naming the missing history even if another urinary condition is recorded, unless the record explicitly excludes both histories, in which case report no finding.
cannot_be_seen: Prostate and bladder symptoms that were never recorded, and past urine retention treated in hospital. Also how strong the anticholinergic effect is for the person at their dose, and supplies from another pharmacy.
ask_the_gp: A review of the antipsychotic in view of the person's prostate or bladder emptying problems, and whether an antipsychotic with weaker anticholinergic effects suits them.
